choices.text: Higher income just slides buyers along the same demand curve to a bigger quantity.
The supply curve shifts right because incomes have risen
A rise in income shifts the whole demand curve right; only a change in the good's own price moves along it.
Demand stays on the same curve and the price never changes

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Higher income just slides buyers along the same demand curve to a bigger quantity. In fact A change in a condition of demand such as income shifts the whole demand curve; only a change in the good's own price moves along it - the shift opens a shortage at the old price, and competition bids the price up along supply to the new equilibrium. The unchanged supply curve stays put while demand shifts from D1 to D2.

questions.answer: A change in a condition of demand such as income shifts the whole demand curve; only a change in the good's own price moves along it - the shift opens a shortage at the old price, and competition bids the price up along supply to the new equilibrium.
